questions.text: What does the statement of cash flows explain?

options.a: Only changes in goodwill balances
options.b: The total market capitalization at a point in time
options.c: Only net income attributable to common shareholders
options.d: Changes in cash resulting from operating, investing, and financing activities during a period

questions.text: Why is a cash flow statement needed in addition to the income statement?

options.a: Accrual earnings do not necessarily equal cash available to meet obligations
options.b: Net income automatically determines the bank balance
options.c: Depreciation is invariably a cash payment
options.d: Revenue is always received immediately in cash

questions.text: What does liquidity mean in the cash flow statement's analytical context?

options.a: Ability to increase share prices
options.b: Ability to eliminate all long-term assets
options.c: Availability of cash to meet short-term obligations
options.d: Ability to earn the highest gross margin

questions.text: What does solvency refer to in the lecture's framework?

options.a: The existence of a patent portfolio
options.b: Only the speed at which inventory is sold
options.c: Only the stability of the dividend yield
options.d: Capacity to meet short-term and long-term obligations

questions.text: What is financial flexibility?

options.a: Capacity to generate or access cash for opportunities and unexpected needs
options.b: The fraction of all shares held by insiders
options.c: The percentage of sales made in foreign currencies
options.d: The length of the depreciation schedule

questions.text: Under IAS 7, operating cash flow broadly relates to what?

options.a: Repaying the face amount of bonds exclusively
options.b: Principal revenue-producing and other operating activities
options.c: Buying production plants exclusively
options.d: Issuing common shares exclusively

questions.text: What is a typical investing cash outflow?

options.a: Paying an employee's monthly salary
options.b: Purchasing a factory for cash
options.c: Issuing new shares for cash
options.d: Receiving cash from customers

questions.text: What is a typical financing cash inflow?

options.a: Selling inventory to a customer
options.b: Collecting a trade receivable
options.c: Obtaining proceeds from a long-term borrowing
options.d: Selling an old production machine

questions.text: How does paying a cash dividend normally appear under the classification used in the course?

options.a: As an investing cash inflow
options.b: As a non-current intangible asset
options.c: As an operating cash receipt
options.d: As a financing cash outflow

questions.text: What is the formula for total cash flow used in the lecture?

options.a: Revenue - Cost of goods sold
options.b: CFO + CFI + CFF
options.c: Net income + Dividends
options.d: Assets - Liabilities

questions.text: What is the main difference between the direct and indirect CFO methods?

options.a: Direct uses market values and indirect uses tax rates
options.b: Direct reports operating cash receipts and payments, while indirect reconciles accounting earnings to operating cash
options.c: The two methods describe different underlying operating cash totals
options.d: Direct covers investing and indirect covers financing only

questions.text: What is the usual starting point of the indirect CFO method?

options.a: Total assets
options.b: Net income or profit
options.c: The maturity value of bonds
options.d: Closing common share price

questions.text: Why is depreciation generally added back in the indirect CFO reconciliation?

options.a: It represents cash borrowed from a bank
options.b: It was omitted from profit despite being a cash payment
options.c: It reduced profit without representing current-period operating cash outflow
options.d: It is a dividend paid to owners

questions.text: What is the indirect-method cash effect of an increase in accounts receivable, all else equal?

options.a: A financing cash inflow
options.b: No relation to cash receipts from customers
options.c: A reduction in operating cash flow relative to net income
options.d: An increase in operating cash flow relative to net income

questions.text: Why does an increase in inventory generally reduce indirect-method operating cash flow, all else equal?

options.a: Cash is tied up in goods that have not yet been sold
options.b: The firm necessarily issued additional shares
options.c: Inventory gains are classified as dividends
options.d: Inventory can only be bought on permanent credit

questions.text: What is the indirect-method cash effect of an increase in accounts payable, all else equal?

options.a: An investing cash outflow
options.b: A deduction from share premium
options.c: An upward adjustment to cash from operations
options.d: A downward adjustment to cash from operations

questions.text: Why is a gain on sale of equipment typically removed from indirect-method CFO?

options.a: The gain creates no income statement effect
options.b: The gain affects net income, while sale proceeds belong to investing activities
options.c: A gain on equipment is always a financing receipt
options.d: The proceeds must always be recognized as sales revenue

questions.text: Which is an example of cash collected from customers under the direct method?

options.a: Issuance of corporate bonds
options.b: Unrealized revaluation surplus
options.c: Receipts from cash sales and settlement of trade receivables
options.d: Depreciation expense

questions.text: What does the direct method subtract from operating cash receipts?

options.a: Cash paid to suppliers, employees, and other operating parties
options.b: The book value of every share outstanding
options.c: The opening carrying value of goodwill
options.d: The market capitalization of the company

questions.text: Do the direct and indirect CFO methods produce different operating cash flow totals for the same underlying transactions?

options.a: Yes, the direct method must always be higher
options.b: Yes, the methods use mutually exclusive operating definitions
options.c: No, they are alternative presentations of the same operating cash flow
options.d: Yes, the indirect method always ignores liabilities

questions.text: Which cash transaction belongs to cash flow from investing activities in the course?

options.a: Cash received from customers for services
options.b: Cash spent acquiring a new production line
options.c: Cash raised by issuing ordinary shares
options.d: Cash paid to suppliers for inventories

questions.text: What is the cash-flow classification of selling an existing piece of PPE for cash?

options.a: An investing cash inflow
options.b: A shareholder contribution
options.c: An operating cash outflow
options.d: A financing cash inflow

questions.text: Which transaction would normally be classified as a financing outflow?

options.a: Paying cash to buy intangible assets
options.b: Collecting overdue trade receivables
options.c: Paying for raw materials
options.d: Repaying bank-loan principal

questions.text: How does a cash share repurchase affect financing cash flow?

options.a: It creates an investing cash inflow
options.b: It is recorded as revenue
options.c: It creates a financing cash outflow
options.d: It adds to operating cash flow

questions.text: Why are borrowing proceeds not part of net income when the loan is first received?

options.a: Debt proceeds are an increase in gross margin
options.b: Interest expense is eliminated when proceeds arrive
options.c: Borrowing creates a liability rather than earned revenue
options.d: Borrowing represents profit from selling an asset

questions.text: What does a strongly negative CFI often indicate for a growing firm?

options.a: Automatic repayment of all bonds
options.b: An absence of productive capital spending
options.c: Certain business failure
options.d: Substantial investment in long-lived assets and other growth opportunities

questions.text: Why is positive CFI not automatically a favorable sign?

options.a: Positive CFI proves that operations are profitable
options.b: Positive CFI means the firm never made an investment
options.c: Positive CFI must equal an increase in receivables
options.d: It may arise from selling productive assets or liquidating investments

questions.text: What is free cash flow (FCF) as defined in Chapter 5's lecture slides?

options.a: Total cash flow plus dividends
options.b: Only dividends plus share repurchases
options.c: Net income divided by current liabilities
options.d: Cash flow from operations plus cash flow from investing activities

questions.text: Why does the lecture caution against interpreting its simple FCF measure as a complete measure of value creation?

options.a: Cash investment outlays can reduce measured FCF even when they create valuable future assets
options.b: Cash flows cannot be negative for growing firms
options.c: All investment spending destroys economic value
options.d: FCF precisely captures every non-cash benefit

questions.text: What distinguishes cash flow from profitability?

options.a: Cash flow records cash movements; profit reflects accrual recognition of economic performance
options.b: Profit ignores all expenses
options.c: Cash flow and accounting profit are identical by definition
options.d: Cash flow is only the annual change in equity

questions.text: Under Dickinson's cash-flow-sign framework, what pattern characterizes an introductory-stage firm?

options.a: Negative CFO, negative CFI, positive CFF
options.b: Positive CFO, negative CFI, negative CFF
options.c: Negative CFO, positive CFI, negative CFF
options.d: Positive CFO, positive CFI, positive CFF

questions.text: Under Dickinson's framework, what pattern is characteristic of a growth-stage firm?

options.a: Negative CFO, negative CFI, negative CFF
options.b: Negative CFO, positive CFI, negative CFF
options.c: Positive CFO, positive CFI, negative CFF
options.d: Positive CFO, negative CFI, positive CFF

questions.text: Under Dickinson's framework, which sign pattern characterizes a mature firm?

options.a: Positive CFO, negative CFI, negative CFF
options.b: Negative CFO, positive CFI, positive CFF
options.c: Positive CFO, positive CFI, positive CFF
options.d: Negative CFO, negative CFI, positive CFF

questions.text: Which economic story best matches mature-firm cash flow patterns?

options.a: Business operations consume cash and all activities rely on new equity issuance
options.b: There is no need to invest in long-lived assets
options.c: Established operations fund investment and net payments to capital providers
options.d: Assets must always be liquidated to fund ongoing operations

questions.text: Why might a young, fast-growing firm have negative total cash flow despite an attractive business model?

options.a: The firm must have violated accounting standards
options.b: Investment outlays may exceed contemporaneous cash generation and financing
options.c: Negative cash flow proves demand is absent
options.d: Cash flow cannot be negative if sales grow

questions.text: How can financing cash flow assist in identifying a company's stage of development?

options.a: Financing cash flow always increases with age
options.b: All life-cycle stages have identical financing cash flow
options.c: Financing activity consists only of customer collections
options.d: Young firms often raise capital, whereas mature firms may repay debt and distribute cash

questions.text: Why should cash-flow-sign life-cycle classification be treated as a proxy rather than conclusive proof?

options.a: Life-cycle stages can be observed perfectly from one ratio
options.b: Temporary transactions and circumstances can produce misleading sign patterns
options.c: Accounting standards prohibit changing investment policies
options.d: The cash flow statement is never audited

questions.text: What is a possible interpretation of negative CFO combined with positive financing cash flow?

options.a: Operations are necessarily producing record profits in cash
options.b: There is no financing dependence
options.c: Operations are consuming cash and external funding is supporting the firm
options.d: The firm is paying all debt off immediately

questions.text: Why can a business with positive CFO nevertheless experience a fall in cash?

options.a: Inventory cannot affect cash balances
options.b: Investing and financing outflows may exceed CFO
options.c: Depreciation must always consume cash
options.d: All positive CFO must increase cash

questions.text: Why do analysts compare CFO with debt commitments?

options.a: Debt cannot be repaid with cash generated from operations
options.b: Share price alone determines loan repayment ability
options.c: Cash generation is crucial for actual interest and principal payments
options.d: Accounting profit can always be used directly as money

questions.text: What is the practitioner approximation to operating cash flow shown in the lecture?

options.a: Revenue - Operating expenses + Share price
options.b: Net income + Depreciation + Amortization + Pension provisions
options.c: Cash from investing + Cash from financing
options.d: Dividends + Equity issues - Borrowings

questions.text: Why does the lecturer describe the simple practitioner operating-cash-flow formula as crude?

options.a: It omits important working-capital movements and other non-cash adjustments
options.b: It includes future cash receipts from every new project
options.c: It is mathematically identical to audited CFO under all circumstances
options.d: It adjusts fully for every cash and non-cash item

questions.text: What does a decrease in accrued operating expenses generally do in an indirect CFO reconciliation?

options.a: It becomes an investing inflow
options.b: It reduces operating cash flow relative to net income
options.c: It has no cash effect regardless of payment
options.d: It raises operating cash flow relative to net income

questions.text: What is the cash flow classification of collecting principal on a loan granted to another company under the course's general IAS 7 treatment?

options.a: An operating cash outflow from wages
options.b: A dividend paid to shareholders
options.c: A financing cash inflow from bond issuance
options.d: An investing cash inflow

questions.text: What is the cash flow classification of buying an ownership stake in another company for investment purposes?

options.a: Operating inflow from customers
options.b: Investing outflow
options.c: Financing inflow from issuing shares
options.d: Other comprehensive income only

questions.text: What is one major use of cash flow statements for credit analysis?

options.a: Measuring only the number of outstanding patents
options.b: Assessing whether operating cash can cover financing and other cash needs
options.c: Determining the board's gender composition
options.d: Guaranteeing that interest rates will decline

questions.text: Why might a firm have accounting profit but insufficient liquidity?

options.a: Profit includes non-cash accruals and cash may be tied up in working capital or investments
options.b: Profit legally requires immediate collection of all receivables
options.c: Every profitable sale is paid in cash on the same date
options.d: Liquidity and solvency are identical to profit

questions.text: How does an increase in prepaid expenses generally affect indirect-method CFO?

options.a: It reduces total shares outstanding
options.b: It increases cash from borrowing
options.c: It increases CFO relative to net income
options.d: It reduces CFO relative to net income

questions.text: When selling a machine for cash above its carrying amount, which presentation is consistent with the indirect method?

options.a: Classify the sale proceeds as financing inflow
options.b: Subtract the disposal gain from CFO and show the cash proceeds in CFI
options.c: Add the full sales proceeds to both CFO and CFI
options.d: Ignore both the gain and the proceeds

questions.text: What limitation arises when using the sign of CFI alone to assess investment quality?

options.a: Cash outflows do not reveal whether the projects have positive net present value
options.b: Positive CFI always means future growth is strong
options.c: All negative investing cash flows are harmful
options.d: The sign of CFI reports the expected return exactly

questions.text: Why can major acquisitions make cash-flow patterns difficult to interpret?

options.a: Acquisitions cannot affect cash flow
options.b: Acquisition outflows must be classified as dividends
options.c: Acquisitions always increase operating cash flow immediately
options.d: Large one-off investing outflows may dominate otherwise normal period cash flows

questions.text: What is the effect of repaying outstanding debt with cash?

options.a: Investing cash inflow and lower PPE
options.b: Operating cash inflow and higher retained earnings
options.c: Financing cash outflow and a reduction in the debt liability
options.d: A simultaneous increase in cash and debt

questions.text: What cash-flow pattern best supports a claim of internally financed operating sustainability?

options.a: Recurring positive CFO sufficient to support necessary reinvestment and obligations
options.b: Persistent reliance on new borrowings to pay all operating expenses
options.c: Consistently negative CFO with no accessible external capital
options.d: A large gain from selling a one-time asset

questions.text: Why are classification policies relevant when comparing cash flow statements of different companies?

options.a: Some payments, such as interest and dividends under IAS 7, may have permitted presentation alternatives subject to standards and policy choices
options.b: Classification never affects CFO comparability
options.c: Operating cash flow must always equal EBITDA
options.d: Every jurisdiction must use identical presentation for every possible cash payment

questions.text: A firm shows net profit of €100 million, a €30 million rise in receivables, and €20 million depreciation, ignoring other adjustments. What is the implied indirect-method CFO?

options.a: €50 million
options.b: €110 million
options.c: €150 million
options.d: €90 million

questions.text: A firm generates CFO of €120 million, spends €80 million net on investing activities, and repays €60 million net in financing activities. What happens to total cash flow before exchange effects?

options.a: It increases by €100 million
options.b: It increases by €40 million
options.c: It decreases by €20 million
options.d: It decreases by €140 million

questions.text: A company sells a warehouse for cash and repays a bank loan with the proceeds. How are the two cash flows typically classified?

options.a: Sale in investing activities; principal repayment in financing activities
options.b: Both in operating activities
options.c: Both in other comprehensive income
options.d: Sale in financing; principal repayment in investing

questions.text: A company reports negative CFO and negative CFI but positive CFF. Which life-cycle pattern best matches Dickinson's model?

options.a: The standard growth pattern
options.b: Decline
options.c: Maturity
options.d: Introduction

questions.text: Two companies have identical CFO but different free cash flow as defined in the course. What most directly explains the difference?

options.a: Their auditors use different materiality thresholds
options.b: Their dividend payout ratios must be identical
options.c: Their net investing cash flows differ
options.d: Their nominal share values differ

questions.text: A firm improves current reported profit by delaying payments to suppliers. Which caution is most relevant?

options.a: Operating cash flow cannot be affected by working-capital timing
options.b: The improvement necessarily raises long-run gross margin
options.c: Delayed supplier payments are always a financing cash inflow
options.d: Cash from operations may improve temporarily without an equivalent improvement in underlying profitability
